note: The obvious case. If a retriever gets this wrong, it is broken.

Clams are the point: they spoil fast and no other recipe uses them, so this one has to come out. Cacao is deliberate noise. Aglio and prezzemolo were added on 02/08 to lift coverage from 33% to 67%: the original pantry demanded a recipe the user had 2 ingredients out of 6 for.
Carbonara wants guanciale, the user has prosciutto crudo. It's not the classic dish, but it's saved food.
The recipe asks for tuorli, the user has uova (tuorli -> uova). This query is the only way to prove the retriever actually uses derives_from.
Two ingredients. Caprese is the only real match
Eight ingredients spanning two dishes. Both Pasta al pomodoro and Pizza Margherita should come out.
Only the four is_staple ingredients. Every recipe uses at least one of these, so if a retriever counts them in the score, everything wins.
Nothing uses cacao + capperi, and nothing comes close. The honest answer is nothing.
Free pick. Insalata di riso needs succo-di-limone, the user has limone (succo-di-limone -> limone): a second derives_from path the set otherwise never exercises. Also a second non-pasta case.

Ranking test, and the only query whose outcome I cannot predict. Both risottos share five ingredients with this pantry, so a retriever that counts matches ties them while one that scores by proportion puts Milanese ahead. Milanese is the closer of the two and goes in expected; Funghi is the runner-up.

Three legume-and-vegetable soups within 17 points of each other, the closest thing to a real ranking problem in the dataset. Ribollita leads and goes in expected, the other two are genuine runners-up. Ribollita also wants stale bread, which a flat list of keys cannot express, so that requirement is invisible here.

Two dishes of different kinds nearly tied: Parmigiana matches five ingredients, Pizza three, but in proportion they are 62% against 60%. Parmigiana leads and goes in expected. Whoever ranks Pizza first is not wrong, which is why it is acceptable rather than absent.

Chicken plus a soffritto. The soffritto (onion, carrot, celery) shows up in half the dataset, so this doubles as a precision test: a retriever that rewards common vegetables will drag in Minestrone and Pasta al Forno.
Baking staples. Torta di Mele is the answer, but farina, uova and burro also pull Gnocchi and Cotoletta to 50%, which is the trap: those are savoury dishes reached through generic ingredients.
Fish course, a category nothing else in the set touches. Honest note: the answer is obvious and every retriever will find it. It is here for coverage, not to separate the candidates.

Side dish, the last uncovered category, and the only pantry in the set that matches a recipe completely (4/4). It tests nothing about ranking. It does check one thing: that a perfect match actually comes out first.
